column1: # app-bundles.tsv — classic Macintosh archivers and encoders, and the
# creator and BNDL each one actually carries, read from the application.
# One row per BNDL of every application in every copy examined. A stub
# claims a CREATOR, so this is the evidence for which creators exist and
# what each application says its documents are (DECISIONS.md 2026-10-12,
#   query         what was searched for (harvest/queries.txt), or "local"
#   application   the application's name as it was found
#   creator       the application file's creator — what the Finder hands
#   bundle_owner  the BNDL's owner; an application may carry bundles for
#                 creators that are not its own (StuffIt Expander's for
#                 SIT!), which paint icons and open nothing
#   declared_types the FREF types of that BNDL, in order
#                 + the path is the original, served as MacBinary — or
#                 local:<image>, a disk image in ~/.cache/macextract built
#                 by tools/vmac from the vendors' own distributions
#   sha256        of the MacBinary as downloaded (discmaster rows)
# "(no application found)": the copy could not be opened — usually a row
# Discmaster itself could not extract, or a PowerPC-only build.
